mike: Quick dump from yesterday's prod-replay on rwd-serve-ptx1. Ran perfetto + nsys, stitched traces. TL;DR: prefix/KV reuse for mid-length requests (~32-64 tokens) dropped ~30% vs baseline; seeing an unexpected memcpy hotspot and a cutlass matmul variant that has low SM utilization. Putting raw notes below.

sana: Can you paste the nsys/perfetto commands and the short KV stats? Want to reproduce locally. :eyes:

mike: Sure — commands I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=run_2026_03_17.nsys-rep \
  ./tools/replay --model=redwood-v1 --workload=prod_replay --seed=42

# perfetto (host timeline)
perfetto --config perfetto_cfg.pbtxt -o perfetto_2026_03_17.trace
```
Short extracted KV/prefix metrics from the replay (5m window):
- KV cache overall hit rate: 48.3%
- Cold misses (never seen in window): 28.1%
- Eviction-induced misses: 23.6%
Baseline (last good run): 72.1% hit rate.

mike: From the nsys GPU timeline:
- ~12 ms of memcpy H2D overlapping only partially with compute.
- cutlass::matmul_f16 kernel selected for several batches that used small M/K/N (underfill).
- aten::layer_norm_kernel shows up as many ~0.8-1.2ms small launches (fragmentation).
- Overall compute time increased ~14% per token for affected batches.

jules: Did the kernel selection table change recently? The cutlass selector has a new fallback for small shapes right?

mike: Not intentionally. I inspected the selector logs, and for those shapes the selector chose the 'small-tile' cutlass path which on this GPU (A100S) gives poor occupancy. There was also a subtle change in batch composition: we started grouping arrivals by time only, ignoring seq-length buckets (recent PR). That increases chance that a mid-length seq sits in a batch dominated by short sequences -> lower KV prefix reuse.

zhou: That matches the hit-rate drop. If many short sequences are first in batch, their prefixes pollute cache windows and evictions spike for mids. Do we have an eviction timeline?

mike: I exported an eviction heatmap (perfetto slice): eviction pressure peaks align with high arrival bursts. Rough numbers from trace: eviction events/sec up ~2.2x, correlated with batches where average seq len < 16 but max seq len > 40.

sana: So two problems: bad kernel chosen for those shape combos + batching heuristic causing low reuse. Which is higher impact?

mike: From sensitivity: switching kernel (force the 'large-tile' matmul) on a sample reduced compute time by ~22% for those batches, improving token latency ~6%. Fixing batching to be seq-aware (group by histogram lane) increased KV hit to ~65% in an A/B run, giving another ~8% token latency improvement. Both needed.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: model=redwood-v1, metric=median_token_latency, delta=+9.2% vs baseline (2026-03-10). Triggered at 2026-03-17T21:10:04Z. Related traces: run_2026_03_17.nsys-rep, perfetto_2026_03_17.trace

jules: Action items: 1) Add debug flag to force kernel path on a canary pool (mike). 2) Rollback PR that changed batch assembly OR implement adaptive lane grouping (sana + zhou). 3) Re-run replay with elevated KV capacity (no-eviction config) to confirm eviction sensitivity (mike).

sana: I'll take the batching patch. Plan: implement adaptive assembler that prefers same seq-length buckets up to latency T, otherwise fallback. I'll add metrics: per-batch avg_seq, max_seq, KV_hit_post_batch.

mike: I'll queue two repro jobs: (A) force matmul path + current batching; (B) adaptive batching + default kernel selector. I'll attach nsys slices and eviction traces. ETA ~ EOD.

zhou: I'll make an automated perfetto query to extract H2D memcpy durations per batch and stack them against kernel occupancy. Quick query snippet to run locally:
```
# perfetto trace_processor SQL (sketch)
SELECT batch_id, SUM(slice.dur)/1000 as memcpy_ms, AVG(kernel.occupancy)
FROM slice JOIN kernel ON slice.track_id = kernel.track_id
WHERE slice.name LIKE 'memcpy_H2D%'
GROUP BY batch_id
ORDER BY memcpy_ms DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

sana: Perfect. @mike once you upload the nsys rep I'll pull the flame charts. We'll aim to have a canary by tomorrow AM. :rocket:

mike: Uploaded artifacts to /mnt/artifacts/run_2026_03_17/{nsys,perfetto,kv-metrics.csv}. Putting minimal reproducer in #eng-runtime later.

jules: Nice investigative thread. Keep updates brief in thread. If canary looks good, we can roll the kernel selector override for 10% traffic then enable batching change behind feature flag.

sana: noted. Adding ticket now.
